title: Efficient Electrocatalytic Reduction of CO2 to HCOOH by Bimetallic In-Cu Nanoparticles with Controlled Growth Facet
abstract: The electrochemical reduction of CO2 to formic acid (HCOOH) by Indium (In)-based materials have been considered an effective way to solve the energy crisis. Unfortunately, In-based materials face a low selectivity for HCOOH in CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR) systems. Here, we have successfully prepared bimetallic InxCuy (x, y are the molar ratio) nanoparticles (NPs) electrocatalysts. For the first time, we adjust the growth direction of the electrocatalysts crystal facets by changing the In/Cu ratio in the electrocatalysts structure, so that the Faraday efficiency of HCOOH by In-based materials are raised to a new level (90% at -1.2 V vs. RHE). Indeed, DFT calculations further showed that the In (101) facet of in InxCuy NPs stabilizes the *OCHO intermediate more effectively, thereby reducing the potential for CO2 to HCOOH. The insights gained from this work can lay the foundation for designing efficient electrocatalysts for the reduction of CO2 to HCOOH.

sections.text:

renewable energy contribute to establishing an artificial carbon-neutral cycle that can
control the greenhouse effect effectively and alleviate the rapid consumption of fossil
fuels[1-3]. Among the various products of the electrochemical CO2RR, HCOOH has been regarded as one of the most attractive fuels due to its high volumetric hydrogen
density, nontoxicity, safety, and transportability[4,5]. It is important to develop an
electrocatalyst capable of reducing CO2 to a high value-added HCOOH with high efficiency, good selectivity, and long-term stability[6]. Indium (In), a non-noble metal,
is attractive due to its intrinsic catalytic activity to produce HCOOH[7]. However, it
usually faces a low selectivity for HCOOH in both organic and aqueous CO2RR systems[8]. Therefore, it is essential to improve the product selectivity of the In-based
CO2RR electrocatalyst.
Bimetallic electrocatalysts, which could bring extra synergistic effects, stabilize
the reaction intermediates, or the suppression of hydrogen and CO production, is
efficient to improve the selectivity and activity of the CO2RR[9]. Increasingly researchers focus on combining other metals with In to achieve bimetallic In-based
electrocatalysts, which could exhibit highly selective, stable performance and low
overpotential[10,11]. Bimetallic In-Cu electrocatalyst is one of the promising
electrocatalysts for CO2RR with enhanced performance for product production[12-14]. For instance, the use of Cu-In alloy to improve the selectivity of the CO2RR, that is, dendritic Cu-In alloy electrode by electrodeposition method produces HCOOH with
high efficiency by CO2RR[15]. Besides, by changing the ratio of Cu and In, the Cu-In catalyst can be adjusted from a core-shell structure that selectively produces CO to a
hybrid structure that prefers HCOOH[16]. As different kinds of electrocatalysts are
successfully synthesized, it is extremely important to further improve their performance.
It has been reported that the adjustment of the size and morphology of the metal
electrocatalysts could control the number of active sites on the electrocatalysts surface
and stabilize the reaction intermediate[17-19]. In addition, the structure of the
bimetallic electrocatalysts can be fine-tuned to stabilize the reaction intermediate more
effectively by controlling the growth direction of the crystal facet, thereby reducing the
potential for CO2RR and further improving the electrocatalytic performance. For

example, by adjusting the crystal structure of the hierarchical hexagonal Zn catalyst to
control (101)/(002) facet ratio of Zn, the electrocatalyst is preferentially grown along
with the Zn (101) facet, thereby promoting the efficient and stable production of CO[20].
Similarly, Qin et al. reported the electrochemical reduction of CO2 to syngas by regulating the growth direction of the Zn electrocatalysts crystal facets[21]. However,
these reported controllable growth facets are restricted to pure metal electrocatalysts.
There is no relevant research about controlling the growth direction of crystal facet for
the unalloyed phase in bimetallic electrocatalysts.
Herein, we successfully designed an in-situ growth method to prepare a series of
bimetallic InxCuy NPs electrocatalysts. For the first time, we adjust the growth direction of the electrocatalysts crystal facets by changing the In/Cu ratio in the electrocatalysts
structure. And then we can tune the main products of the CO2RR from both CO and HCOOH to HCOOH. When the molar ratio of In and Cu is 1.5:0.5, the In1.5Cu0.5 NPs electrocatalysts preferentially grow along with the In (101) facet. In electrochemical
analysis, only the In (101) facet of in In1.5Cu0.5 NPs is favorable to HCOOH formation. The Faraday efficiency (FE) of HCOOH can reach 90% at -1.2 V vs. RHE (reversible
hydrogen electrode), outperforming than most reported In-Cu materials[15,16]. We
extend the Grazing incidence X-ray diffractometer (GIXRD) analysis to analyze the
detail orientations difference of a series of the InxCuy NPs surfaces. Furthermore, the origin of the catalytic selectivity of the electrochemical CO2RR of the InxCuy NPs structure was analyzed by density functional theory (DFT) calculations.

above solutions under magnetic stirring, and then 0.2128 g of carbon black (CB) was

sections.heading: 2.3.1 Electrode preparation
sections.text:
Before the experiment, all the carbon papers (CPs) were sonicated deionized water
for 30 min. To prepare the InxCuy NPs electrode, 5.0 mg InxCuy NPs prepared were suspended in 1.0 mL ethanol with 40 μL Nafion D-521 dispersion (5 wt%) to form a
homogeneous ink assisted by ultrasound. Then, 200 μL of the ink was evenly dropped
onto the CP (1.0 cm×2.0 cm) surface by a micropipette and then dried at 60 °C. The loading of InxCuy NPs was 0.24 mg cm -2.

sections.heading: 2.3.2 Electrochemical measurements
sections.text:
All electrochemical measurements were carried out in H-type electrolytic cells
with 50 mL electrolyte in the cathode and anode, respectively, and separated by Nafion
115 membrane. The InxCuy NPs electrode as the working electrode. Ag/AgCl electrode was used as the reference electrode and the Pt sheet electrode (1.0 cm×1.0 cm) was
used as the counter electrode. CHI660C electrochemical workstation was used to
perform the electrochemical measurements. The electrode potential was converted to

sections.heading: 4. Conclusion
sections.text:
In summary, we developed the In1.5Cu0.5 NPs, which electrochemical reduction of
CO2 to HCOOH with high activity and selectivity (the FEHCOOH is 90% at -1.2 V vs. RHE) as well as high stability. We calculated the texture coefficient of each (hkl) facet
by GIXRD data. Significantly, we found that the FEHCOOH of the InxCuy NPs showed a good positive correlation with the texture coefficient of In (101) facet of in the InxCuy NPs. In particular, DFT calculations showed that the reduction potential of HCOOH
produced by electrochemical reduction CO2 from the In (101) facet of in the InxCuy NPs was lower than that of the CuO (111) facet, indicating that the In (101) facet of in
the InxCuy NPs was more suitable for HCOOH production. Furthermore, for the first time, we propose that changing the molar ratio of the InxCuy NPs to regulate the growth direction of the electrocatalyst crystal facets can be used as a crucial control factor for
product selectivity, achieved the selectivity for different useful products at high levels
can be tuned. And the synthesis method of the In1.5Cu0.5 NPs is simple and it has high selectivity and good stability. Therefore, the In1.5Cu0.5 NPs can be a promising electrocatalyst in practical applications of CO2RR. And this study could provide design principles for further development of other advanced CO2 electrocatalysts.
